summary: All four planned deliverables were produced and the core objective — piping the KDL spec over stdin to the external `usage` CLI via a shared `readUsageSpec()` helper — was correctly implemented in `usageSpec.ts`, `completions.ts`, `usage.ts`, and `scripts/smoke-binary.sh`. Two deviations are present: (1) `tests/unit/architecturalGuards.test.ts` was edited to add `usageSpec.ts` to `CLI_DIRECT_IO_ALLOWLIST`, a mechanical necessity because the new file uses `node:fs` directly and the guard's "kept honest" sub-test would otherwise fail; (2) the smoke-binary.sh invocation for the JSON check uses `--usage --usage-format json` instead of the plan's `--usage-format json`, because `main.ts` only processes `--usage-format` inside the `--usage` dispatch branch. Both deviations are justified and fully documented in phase-handoff.md.

findings.message: Objective fully delivered: readUsageSpec() created with the exact planned return shape; completions.ts and usage.ts JSON branch invoke `usage … -f -` with spec content via spawnSync input; KDL branch writes spec.content directly; smoke-binary.sh asserts both binary paths under a usage-available guard.
Excluded scope respected: no changes to spec generation, deno compile embedding, phax.usage.kdl, phax.json, or the phax --usage (KDL) path.

tests/unit/architecturalGuards.test.ts was edited but not listed in any planned or optional file category. The edit adds usageSpec.ts to CLI_DIRECT_IO_ALLOWLIST, which is mandatory because usageSpec.ts imports node:fs directly and the guard's "kept honest" sub-test requires the allowlist entry. Justified and documented in phase-handoff.md.

tests/integration/completions.test.ts was edited; it is listed as an optional file in the plan. The edit adds the #compdef phax|_phax marker assertion to the zsh test, matching the plan's "optionally tighten an assertion" guidance.

All promised test layers are present: smoke-binary.sh asserts completions zsh and --usage --usage-format json on the compiled binary with usage-available guard and SKIP lines; completions.test.ts retains all prior assertions and gains the zsh marker assertion.

smoke-binary.sh invokes `./dist/bin/phax --usage --usage-format json` instead of the plan's `./dist/bin/phax --usage-format json`. The --usage flag is required because main.ts only processes --usage-format inside the --usage dispatch branch. Justified and documented in phase-handoff.md.
usageSpec.ts stays within src/cli/commands/; no architectural layer boundary crossed. infra/ports/app/domain layers are untouched.
Commit subject fix(cli): pipe usage spec over stdin so completions work in the binary matches the plan exactly.

phase-handoff.md covers all required content: readUsageSpec() path and return shape, confirmation of stdin invocation in completions.ts and usage.ts, smoke-binary.sh guard and skip behaviour, and a documented explanation of the unplanned architecturalGuards.test.ts edit.

attentionPoints: --usage-format json requires --usage to be present on the command line (main.ts only processes --usage-format inside the --usage dispatch branch). The plan assumed standalone --usage-format json would work; the smoke script and real usage both need --usage --usage-format json. Worth verifying whether standalone --usage-format is intentionally unsupported or an undocumented coupling.

CI environments without `usage` on PATH skip both new binary smoke checks (completions zsh and --usage-format json), so the regression guard is not exercised in those environments. Consider ensuring usage is available in CI to get full coverage.
